// diagnostic

E0150

`{op}` needs `{type}` in state `{required}`, but `{value}` is in state `{current}`.

What

`{op}` needs `{type}` in state `{required}`, but `{value}` is in state `{current}`.

Why

Typestate: an operation is valid only in a given state; calling it out of order is the bug typestate prevents.

Fix

Transition the value into `{required}` first — call the transition that reaches it (e.g. `pay` to reach `Confirmed`).

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0150: Tests/UI/Typestate/enum_arm_narrows_to_its_case.stderr.

Error [jet.TypestateWrongState]: `open` needs `Door.Shut`, but `door` is `Door.Locked`
  --> Tests/UI/Typestate/enum_arm_narrows_to_its_case.jet:22:28
    |
 22 |         .Locked(_) -> door.open()
    |                            ^^^^
 Why: Typestate: `open` takes only `Door.Shut`; calling it with `Door` in another state is the out-of-order bug the state list rules out
 Fix: Bring `door` to `Door.Shut` before calling `open`
